packageRules.description: Hold TypeScript at 6.x. TypeScript 7.0 is the Go-native compiler and shipped without a stable programmatic API, so typescript-eslint, ts-api-utils and @swc-node/register cannot run on it - Nx fails to build its project graph, which takes lint, test and build down together. Angular's compiler-cli independently requires typescript >=6.0 <6.1, so no TypeScript version satisfies both Angular 22 and a v7 bump. 6.x is deliberately still allowed: it is the actual upgrade path to Angular 22. Revisit when typescript-eslint and @swc-node/register ship v7 support and Angular's compiler-cli accepts it.
Batch JavaScript dependencies managed through npm, pnpm, or Yarn

Batch dependencies published from the Sneat-Co GitHub organization. Own libraries are never gated: the fleet must be on the latest sneat-co release always (founder rule 2026-09-02); third parties keep the weekly window and the 1-day release age above. Note that matchSourceUrls can only match a datasource whose source URL is known -- in practice Go modules, whose module path is the repository URL. npm @sneat/* packages publish no `repository` field, so they are covered by the sibling matchPackageNames rule below, not by this one.

The same exemption as above, matched by PACKAGE NAME because the rule above cannot reach npm. matchSourceUrls resolves against the `repository` field of a package's registry metadata, and NO @sneat/* npm package publishes one (verified 2026-09-03: @sneat/core, @sneat/extension-calendarius-ui, @sneat/extension-calendarius and @sneat/extension-calendarius-contract all return an empty repository.url). So the source-URL exemption only ever applied to Go modules, whose datasource IS the source URL. npm @sneat/* packages fell through to the JavaScript-dependencies group, the weekly Monday window and the 1-day release age -- and internalChecksFilter=strict hid them from the Dependency Dashboard entirely while they waited, so the gap was invisible rather than merely slow.
Auto-merge dependency updates once checks pass.
